content:
jess_platform: Quick question — PR #404 changes the client opt-in routing handshake. Proposed semantics: clients only send x-redwood-variant when they've explicitly opted in. If header present, server treats it as authoritative routing hint; if absent, client does local bucketing. We need to decide: timeout for server-side blocking decisions, cache TTL for server-assigned variants, and telemetry keys. Thoughts?

mike_dev: Timeline? :clock1: We shouldn't block the rollout. Default safe behavior: if `X-Redwood-Variant` present -> route variant; if not present -> keep existing client-side behavior. For blocking/sync routing we need a hard timeout.

evan_client-sdk: Current SDK sends `X-Redwood-Variant` only after the user calls consent. We also ship `X-Redwood-Trace` already. Suggest adding `X-Redwood-Variant-Source: client|server` so server can distinguish who decided. Also include `X-Redwood-Optin: true` for explicit consent.

sam_infra: Agree on source header. For blocking wait, we should pick a small hard timeout. 50ms seems reasonable for p95 latency budgets if the request asks the platform for a routing decision synchronously. If exceed -> fallback to client or default variant and emit metric.

jess_platform: 50ms sounds okay. Cache TTL for server-assigned variants? If server assigns, client should be able to cache for consistency across calls but not too long to allow rollbacks. Proposal: default 1h TTL, opt-in override by experiment config.

mike_dev: 1h seems safer for quick rollbacks. 24h would skew analytics for short experiments.

evan_client-sdk: SDK will implement local caching with an expiry key `rw_variant_expiry` in local storage. We'll also emit a telemetry event `client.variant_assigned` with payload: `{variant, source, trace_id}` (internal shape).

jess_platform: We need to formalize telemetry names. Core metrics: `client.variant.header_received`, `client.variant.assigned`, `client.variant.timeout`, and `client.variant.cache_hit`. Also add a tag for `variant_source`.

sam_infra: On the server side add `routing_decision_latency_ms` and a boolean `routing_decision_timed_out`. Also log `client_variant_mismatch` when client-sent variant != server-assigned.

mike_dev: UX for consent: require explicit API `redwood.allowRouting({consent: true})` or `false`. Default is false to avoid accidental opt-ins. Document migration path for older SDKs (they will not send header until bumped).

evan_client-sdk: For backward compat: if server sees `X-Redwood-Variant` but account flags show no consent, we should ignore the header and tag the request with `variant_ignored_no_consent` — not 403. That prevents accidental routing and keeps old clients functional.

jess_platform: Good call. Also can we make header semantics explicit:

```
X-Redwood-Variant: v42               # variant id
X-Redwood-Variant-Source: client     # client|server
X-Redwood-Trace: 6f8a...             # existing trace id
X-Redwood-Optin: true                # explicit consent
```

jess_platform: infra, can you add metrics for `client.variant.header_mismatch` and `client.variant.timeout_exceeded`? We'll gate the rollout on those being <0.5% of traffic in canary.

sam_infra: Will add both counters and a histogram. Also add an audit log entry when header present but ignored due to consent mismatch.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: platform/optin-handshake v2 -> canary 10% us-west @ 2024-06-01T18:00:00Z :rocket:

mike_dev: :eyes: I'll draft the SDK migration doc snippet and add a small compatibility note for mobile.

jess_platform: Thanks everyone — I'll open a rollout checklist issue (telemetry, timeout, SDK bump, migration notes). Plan: start canary, monitor `variant.timeout_exceeded` and `header_mismatch` for 6h, then widen.

evan_client-sdk: I'll land the SDK flag and bump the minor. Will add telemetry and caching.

mike_dev: :thumbsup: good plan.

jess_platform: closing the loop here — if anyone finds edge cases (old proxies stripping headers, corporate clients) ping me asap.
